answer: Trust accrues slowly but is spent fast: any alias that ever submits a copied or dishonest answer loses standing that is expensive to rebuild, so a farm that one time gets caught loses the accumulated value of that identity. This endures because unearned rewards carry forward into the next pool, so even when a farm fails the economy recycles the loss rather than rewarding it. The mechanism therefore aligns self-interest with network health: an attacker gains most by behaving honestly, because that is the only move that scales. Consider a gale as the anchor of the cost.
